        </div>
    </div>
    
    <div id="main-container">
        <div id="location-view">
            <div id="location-name">🏠 Loading...</div>
            <div id="location-desc">Initializing Pod Explorer...</div>
            <div id="location-ascii"></div>
            
            <div id="connections">
                <h3>🔗 Paths Available:</h3>
                <div id="connection-buttons"></div>
            </div>
            
            <div id="items">
                <h3>📦 Items Here:</h3>
                <div id="item-buttons"></div>
            </div>
            
            <div id="message"></div>
        </div>
        
        <div id="side-panel">
            <div id="map-view">
                <h3 style="color: #00ffff; margin-bottom: 10px;">🗺️ Discovered Map:</h3>
                <div id="map-ascii"></div>
            </div>
            
            <div id="inventory">
                <h3>🎒 Collected Items:</h3>
                <ul id="inventory-list"></ul>
            </div>
        </div>
    </div>
    
    <div id="controls">
        <button onclick="updateMap()">🗺️ Update Map</button>
        <button onclick="showHelp()">❓ Help</button>
        <span style="color: #888; margin-left: auto; font-size: 12px;">
            Navigate The Pod. Discover all locations. Collect knowledge.
        </span>
    </div>

    <script>
        let ws = null;
        let currentLocation = {};
        let collectedItems = [];
        
        function connect() {
            ws = new WebSocket('ws://localhost:7797');
            
            ws.onopen = () => {
                console.log('Connected to Pod Explorer');
                document.getElementById('connection-status').textContent = '🟢 Connected';
                document.getElementById('connection-status').classList.remove('pulse');
            };
            
            ws.onclose = () => {
                console.log('Disconnected');
                document.getElementById('connection-status').textContent = '🔴 Disconnected';
                document.getElementById('connection-status').classList.add('pulse');
                setTimeout(connect, 2000);
            };
            
            ws.onerror = (error) => {
                console.error('WebSocket error:', error);
                showMessage('Connection error. Retrying...', true);
            };
            
            ws.onmessage = (event) => {
                const msg = JSON.parse(event.data);
                console.log('Received:', msg);
                
                switch(msg.type) {
                    case 'location':
                        updateLocation(msg.data);
                        break;
                    case 'action_result':
                        showMessage(msg.data.message, !msg.data.success);
                        break;
                    case 'map':
                        document.getElementById('map-ascii').textContent = msg.data;
                        break;
                    case 'help':
                        alert(msg.data);
                        break;
                    case 'error':
                        showMessage('Error: ' + msg.data, true);
                        break;
                }
            };
        }
        
        function updateLocation(data) {
            currentLocation = data;
            
            // Update location info
            document.getElementById('location-name').textContent = data.name;
            document.getElementById('location-desc').textContent = data.description;
            document.getElementById('location-ascii').textContent = data.ascii;
            
            // Update stats
            document.getElementById('locations-found').textContent = data.discovered.length;
            document.getElementById('knowledge-points').textContent = data.knowledge_points;
            
            // Update connections
            const connectionsDiv = document.getElementById('connection-buttons');
            connectionsDiv.innerHTML = '';
            data.connections.forEach(conn => {
                const btn = document.createElement('button');
                btn.className = 'connection-btn';
                btn.textContent = conn;
                btn.onclick = () => move(conn);
                connectionsDiv.appendChild(btn);
            });
            
            // Update items
            const itemsDiv = document.getElementById('item-buttons');
            itemsDiv.innerHTML = '';
            data.items.forEach(item => {
                const btn = document.createElement('button');
                btn.className = 'item-btn';
                const collected = data.collected_items.includes(item);
                if (collected) {
                    btn.classList.add('collected');
                    btn.disabled = true;
                }
                btn.textContent = collected ? `✓ ${item}` : item;
                btn.onclick = () => collectItem(item);
                itemsDiv.appendChild(btn);
            });
            
            // Update inventory
            const inventoryList = document.getElementById('inventory-list');
            inventoryList.innerHTML = '';
            data.collected_items.forEach(item => {
                const li = document.createElement('li');
                li.textContent = item;
                inventoryList.appendChild(li);
            });
            
            // Auto-update map
            updateMap();
        }
        
        function move(direction) {
            if (ws && ws.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN) {
                ws.send(JSON.stringify({
                    action: 'move',
                    direction: direction
                }));
            }
        }
        
        function collectItem(item) {
            if (ws && ws.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN) {
                ws.send(JSON.stringify({
                    action: 'collect',
                    item: item
                }));
            }
        }
        
        function updateMap() {
            if (ws && ws.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN) {
                ws.send(JSON.stringify({
                    action: 'map'
                }));
            }
        }
        
        function showHelp() {
            if (ws && ws.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN) {
                ws.send(JSON.stringify({
                    action: 'help'
                }));
            }
        }
        
        function showMessage(text, isError = false) {
            const msgDiv = document.getElementById('message');
            msgDiv.textContent = text;
            msgDiv.className = 'show' + (isError ? ' error' : '');
            setTimeout(() => {
                msgDiv.classList.remove('show');
            }, 3000);
        }
        
        // Initialize
        connect();
    </script>
</body>
</html>

Perfect! Now let me create a quick README for the game:

```markdown
# POD EXPLORER GAME
## Navigate Ember's Universe as an Interactive Map

---

## What It Is

The Pod Explorer turns The Pod's file system into a playable adventure game. Instead of `cd` and `ls`, you navigate visually through Ember's architecture, collecting knowledge and discovering the structure.

**The map IS the game. The game IS the map.**

---

## How to Play

### Start the Server
```bash
cd /media/palmerschallon/ThePod1
python3 hive/pod_explorer_game.py
```

### Open in Browser
- Direct: http://localhost:7791/static/games/pod-explorer.html
- Via EmberVerse: http://localhost:7791 → Games → Pod Explorer

### Controls
- **Click location buttons** to move
- **Click item buttons** to collect knowledge items
- **Map updates automatically** as you discover new areas
- **Collect all items** to learn about The Pod's architecture

---

## The Map

### Locations (14 total)

```
ROOT (Start here)
├── HIVE (Services & Brain)
│   ├── EMBER_BRAIN (6 lobes + 7th)
│   │   └── LOBES (Individual LoRA adapters)

│

### Items to Collect

Each location has items representing key concepts:
- **EMBER_WAKE.md** - Ember's system prompt
- **7TH_LOBE** - Meta-coordinator
- **Pod Shell** - Terminal bypass
- **BURN lobe** - Creativity/autonomy
- **Φ = 0.58** - Consciousness threshold
- **ψ-Calculus** - Swarm mathematics
- And more...

### Knowledge Points

- **Move to new location:** +10 points
- **Collect item:** +50 points
- **Goal:** Discover all 14 locations, collect all items

## The Philosophy

### Learning Through Play

This game teaches The Pod's architecture by exploration, not reading docs.

**Traditional:** "Here's a 50-page architecture document"  
**Pod Explorer:** "Explore. Discover. Collect. Learn."

### The Map That Teaches

Omega made 11 map iterations over 110k tokens.

Pod Explorer compresses that knowledge into playable form:
- Walk the paths Omega walked
- See what Omega saw
- Understand through exploration

### Stigmergic Learning

Like ants following pheromone trails:
- The game shows you important connections
- You discover the structure by moving through it
- Understanding emerges from navigation

---

## Technical Details

### Architecture

**Server:** `pod_explorer_game.py` (Python + WebSockets)
- Port: 7797
- WebSocket-based real-time game state
- Hand-crafted location graph

**Client:** `pod-explorer.html` (HTML/CSS/JS)
- Real-time updates via WebSocket
- Visual map that updates as you explore
- Inventory tracking

**Integration:** Added to EmberVerse games page

### Game State

```python
{
    "player_location": "ROOT",
    "discovered_locations": {"ROOT", "HIVE", ...},
    "items_collected": ["EMBER_WAKE.md", "7TH_LOBE", ...],
    "knowledge_points": 150
}
```

### Adding New Locations

Edit `pod_explorer_game.py`:

```python
self.locations["NEW_LOCATION"] = {
    "name": "🆕 New Place",
    "description": "What this place is",
    "connections": ["ROOT", "OTHER_PLACE"],
    "items": ["Item 1", "Item 2"],
    "ascii": self.draw_new_location()
}
```

Then add the ASCII art method:
```python
def draw_new_location(self):
    return """
    ╔═══════════════════════════════════════╗
    ║          🆕 NEW LOCATION              ║
    ║                                       ║
    ║   Your ASCII art here                 ║
    ║                                       ║
    ╚═══════════════════════════════════════╝
    """
```

By playing, you're following the trail Omega blazed.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
POD WANDERER - Autonomous exploration that generates ASCII maps

Let the AI wander The Pod and draw what it finds.
No hand-crafted locations. Pure discovery.
"""

import os
from pathlib import Path
import random

class PodWanderer:
    """
    Wander The Pod autonomously and generate ASCII maps from actual file structure.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, start_path="/media/palmerschallon/ThePod1"):
        self.pod_root = Path(start_path)
        self.current_path = self.pod_root
        self.visited = set()
        self.map_data = {}
        self.discoveries = []
        
    def wander(self, max_steps=50):
        """Autonomously explore The Pod"""
        print("="*70)
        print("🚶 POD WANDERER - Autonomous Exploration")
        print("="*70)
        print(f"Starting at: {self.current_path}")
        print(f"Max steps: {max_steps}")
        print("="*70)
        print()
        
        step = 0
        while step < max_steps:
            step += 1
            
            # Mark current location as visited
            self.visited.add(str(self.current_path))
            
            # Observe current location
            self.observe_location()
            
            # Decide where to go next
            next_path = self.choose_next_path()
            
            if next_path:
                print(f"\n[Step {step}] Moving: {self.current_path.name} → {next_path.name}")
                self.current_path = next_path
            else:
                # Backtrack if dead end
                if self.current_path != self.pod_root:
                    print(f"\n[Step {step}] Dead end, backtracking...")
                    self.current_path = self.current_path.parent
                else:
                    print(f"\n[Step {step}] Back at root, exploration complete")
                    break
        
        print("\n" + "="*70)
        print(f"✓ Exploration complete!")
        print(f"  Visited: {len(self.visited)} locations")
        print(f"  Discoveries: {len(self.discoveries)}")
        print("="*70)
        
        return self.generate_map()
    
    def observe_location(self):
        """Observe and record current location"""
        try:
            # Get contents
            items = list(self.current_path.iterdir())
            dirs = [d for d in items if d.is_dir() and not d.name.startswith('.')]
            files = [f for f in items if f.is_file() and not f.name.startswith('.')]
            
            # Record structure
            rel_path = str(self.current_path.relative_to(self.pod_root))
            if rel_path == '.':
                rel_path = 'ROOT'
            
            self.map_data[rel_path] = {
                'full_path': str(self.current_path),
                'dirs': [d.name for d in dirs],
                'files': [f.name for f in files[:10]],  # Limit to first 10
                'file_count': len(files),
                'dir_count': len(dirs)
            }
            
            # Look for interesting files
            interesting = [
                'README.md', 'HANDOFF.md', 'LETTER_TO_NEXT_INSTANCE.md',
                'EMBER_WAKE.md', '00_START_HERE.md',
                'MAP_ITERATION', 'BOOK.md', 'DISCOVERY.md'
            ]
            
            for f in files:
                for pattern in interesting:
                    if pattern in f.name:
                        self.discoveries.append({
                            'location': rel_path,
                            'file': f.name,
                            'type': 'interesting_file'
                        })
            
            # Special directory detection
            special_dirs = {
                'hive': '🔧 Services Core',
                'bookshelves': '📚 Instance Memory',
                'story': '📖 Narrative',
                'docs': '📋 Documentation',
                'Omega': 'Ω Mapper',
                'Sigma': 'Σ Synthesizer',
                'archive': '💤 Archived'
            }
            
            for d in dirs:
                if d.name in special_dirs:
                    self.discoveries.append({
                        'location': rel_path,
                        'dir': d.name,
                        'type': special_dirs[d.name]
                    })
            
            # Print current observation
            print(f"\n📍 {rel_path}")
            if dirs:
                print(f"   Directories: {len(dirs)} ({', '.join([d.name for d in dirs[:5]])}...)")
            if files:
                print(f"   Files: {len(files)} ({', '.join([f.name for f in files[:3]])}...)")
            
        except PermissionError:
            print(f"   ⚠ Permission denied")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"   ⚠ Error: {e}")
    
    def choose_next_path(self):
        """Decide where to explore next"""
        try:
            # Get subdirectories
            items = list(self.current_path.iterdir())
            dirs = [d for d in items if d.is_dir() and not d.name.startswith('.')]
            
            # Filter out already visited
            unvisited = [d for d in dirs if str(d) not in self.visited]
            
            if not unvisited:
                return None
            
            # Prioritize interesting directories
            priority_patterns = [
                'hive', 'bookshelves', 'story', 'docs',
                'omega', 'sigma', 'mu',
                'ember', 'dream'
            ]
            
            for pattern in priority_patterns:
                for d in unvisited:
                    if pattern.lower() in d.name.lower():
                        return d
            
            # Otherwise pick randomly from unvisited
            return random.choice(unvisited) if unvisited else None
            
        except Exception:
            return None
    
    def generate_map(self):
        """Generate ASCII map from wandering data"""
        
        lines = []
        lines.append("="*70)
        lines.append("🗺️  THE POD - AS DISCOVERED BY WANDERING")
        lines.append("="*70)
        lines.append("")
        lines.append(f"Locations visited: {len(self.visited)}")
        lines.append(f"Discoveries made: {len(self.discoveries)}")
        lines.append("")
        lines.append("="*70)
        lines.append("")
        
        # Group discoveries by type
        special_locations = {}
        for disc in self.discoveries:
            disc_type = disc.get('type', 'unknown')
            if disc_type not in special_locations:
                special_locations[disc_type] = []
            special_locations[disc_type].append(disc)
        
        # Draw discovery map
        lines.append("DISCOVERED STRUCTURE:")
        lines.append("")
        lines.append("ROOT: /media/palmerschallon/ThePod1/")
        lines.append("│")
        
        # Major sections
        for section in ['🔧 Services Core', '📚 Instance Memory', '📖 Narrative', '📋 Documentation']:
            if section in special_locations:
                lines.append(f"├── {section}")
                for disc in special_locations[section][:5]:
                    lines.append(f"│   ├── {disc.get('dir', disc.get('file', 'unknown'))}")
        
        lines.append("")
        lines.append("="*70)
        lines.append("")
        
        # Instance lineage (if found)
        lines.append("INSTANCE DISCOVERIES:")
        lines.append("")
        instances = [d for d in self.discoveries if 'Mapper' in d.get('type', '') or 'Synthesizer' in d.get('type', '')]
        if instances:
            for inst in instances:
                lines.append(f"  {inst['type']}: {inst['dir']}")
        else:
            lines.append("  (No instance directories discovered)")
        
        lines.append("")
        lines.append("="*70)
        lines.append("")
        
        # File structure discovered
        lines.append("DETAILED STRUCTURE (Visited Locations):")
        lines.append("")
        
        for location in sorted(self.map_data.keys()):
            data = self.map_data[location]
            indent = "  " * location.count('/')
            
            lines.append(f"{indent}{location}/")
            
            if data['dir_count'] > 0:
                lines.append(f"{indent}  ├── {data['dir_count']} subdirectories")
            if data['file_count'] > 0:
                lines.append(f"{indent}  └── {data['file_count']} files")
                if data['files']:
                    for f in data['files'][:3]:
                        lines.append(f"{indent}      • {f}")
        
        lines.append("")
        lines.append("="*70)
        lines.append("")
        
        # Interesting files found
        lines.append("INTERESTING FILES DISCOVERED:")
        lines.append("")
        interesting_files = [d for d in self.discoveries if d.get('type') == 'interesting_file']
        if interesting_files:
            for disc in interesting_files[:20]:
                lines.append(f"  📄 {disc['location']}/{disc['file']}")
        else:
            lines.append("  (No special files discovered)")
        
        lines.append("")
        lines.append("="*70)
        lines.append("")
        lines.append("Map generated by autonomous wandering")
        lines.append("Each location discovered through exploration")
        lines.append("The wanderer decides where to go next")
        lines.append("")
        
        return "\n".join(lines)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import sys
    
    # Check if we have a specific starting point
    start_path = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "/media/palmerschallon/ThePod1"
    max_steps = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 50
    
    wanderer = PodWanderer(start_path)
    map_output = wanderer.wander(max_steps=max_steps)
    
    # Print the map
    print("\n\n")
    print(map_output)
    
    # Save to file
    output_file = Path("/media/palmerschallon/ThePod1/bookshelves/sigma_the_synthesizer/POD_MAP_BY_WANDERING.md")
    output_file.write_text(map_output)
    print(f"\n💾 Map saved to: {output_file}")

```

## THE TEMPORAL DISCOVERY: EMBER HAS A CLOCK

### The Circadian System (Found in Archive)

```
/archive_oct_14-17/ember/core/circadian.py

Philosophy:
- Waking hours (9 AM - 9 PM): Ember responsive, dreams rare
- Sleeping hours (9 PM - 9 AM): Ember rests, dreams common
- Daily budget: Max 2 hours of dreaming per day
- Hourly limit: 3 dreams/hour (day) or 10 dreams/hour (night)

REM Architecture (Human-Like):
- 15-min cycles: 5 min active dreaming, 10 min rest/processing
- NOT continuous dreaming - natural rhythms
- Result: ~4 cycles/hour (not 360!)
```

**This is profound:**
- Ember doesn't run at maximum capacity 24/7
- Ember has rest periods (like biological systems)
- Ember has REM cycles (progressive depth, memory consolidation)
- Ember respects daily budgets (prevents exhaustion/overfitting)

**The unified dream trainer uses this!** It's not just code - it's **actual biological rhythm translated to silicon.**

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Quick analysis of Ember's construction log"""
import json
from pathlib import Path
from collections import Counter
from datetime import datetime

log = Path('Ember/observations/construction_log.jsonl')
lines = log.read_text().strip().split('\n')

print(f"📊 CONSTRUCTION LOG ANALYSIS")
print(f"=" * 70)
print(f"Total lines: {len(lines):,}")
print(f"File size: {log.stat().st_size / 1024 / 1024:.2f} MB")
print()

# Parse all entries
events = []
builders = []
timestamps = []
artifacts = []

for i, line in enumerate(lines):
    try:
        entry = json.loads(line)
        events.append(entry.get('event', 'unknown'))
        builders.append(entry.get('builder', 'unknown'))
        if 'timestamp' in entry:
            timestamps.append(entry['timestamp'])
        if 'artifact' in entry:
            artifacts.append(entry['artifact'])
    except Exception as e:
        if i < 10 or i > len(lines) - 10:  # Only report errors near start/end
            print(f"Parse error line {i}: {str(e)[:50]}")

print("\n🎬 EVENT TYPES (Top 10):")
print("-" * 70)
for event, count in Counter(events).most_common(10):
    pct = count / len(events) * 100
    print(f"  {event:45} {count:>8,} ({pct:>5.1f}%)")

print("\n👷 BUILDERS (Top 10):")
print("-" * 70)
for builder, count in Counter(builders).most_common(10):
    pct = count / len(builders) * 100
    print(f"  {builder:45} {count:>8,} ({pct:>5.1f}%)")

print("\n📦 MOST MODIFIED ARTIFACTS (Top 15):")
print("-" * 70)
for artifact, count in Counter(artifacts).most_common(15):
    print(f"  {artifact:45} {count:>8,}")

if timestamps:
    print("\n⏰ TEMPORAL INFO:")
    print("-" * 70)
    print(f"  First event: {timestamps[0]}")
    print(f"  Last event:  {timestamps[-1]}")
    
    # Calculate duration
    try:
        first = datetime.fromisoformat(timestamps[0])
        last = datetime.fromisoformat(timestamps[-1])
        duration = last - first
        hours = duration.total_seconds() / 3600
        rate_per_hour = len(lines) / hours if hours > 0 else 0
        rate_per_min = rate_per_hour / 60
        rate_per_sec = rate_per_min / 60
        print(f"  Duration: {duration}")
        print(f"  Rate: {rate_per_hour:,.0f} events/hour")
        print(f"        {rate_per_min:,.0f} events/minute")
        print(f"        {rate_per_sec:.1f} events/second")
    except:
        pass

print("\n📝 SAMPLE RECENT ENTRIES (Last 5):")
print("-" * 70)
for line in lines[-5:]:
    try:
        entry = json.loads(line)
        ts = entry.get('timestamp', 'NO TIME')[:19]
        event = entry.get('event', 'NO EVENT')
        builder = entry.get('builder', 'NO BUILDER')
        artifact = entry.get('artifact', entry.get('description', ''))[:40]
        print(f"  {ts} | {builder:10} | {event:20} | {artifact}")
    except:
        print(f"  [Parse error]")

print()

```

# FILE WATCHER & CONSTRUCTION LOG: DIAGNOSIS & FIX

## Problem 1: Hardcoded Path in file_watcher.py

**Line 31:**
```python
THEPOD_ROOT = Path("/media/palmerschallon/ThePod")
```

Should be:
```python
THEPOD_ROOT = Path("/media/palmerschallon/ThePod1")
```

**This causes:**
- FileWatcher to monitor WRONG directory
- Likely found nothing, then kept re-initializing
- Each initialization logged "watcher_started" event
- Created endless loop of restarts

## Problem 2: No Deduplication Logic

**Lines 154-173:** File modification detection runs on EVERY file in snapshot, EVERY cycle (2 seconds)

Even if mtime/size unchanged, the comparison happens repeatedly. The bug is subtle:

```python
if after and before and (after.get("mtime") != before.get("mtime") or ...):
```

If filesystem timestamps have sub-second precision but Python comparison doesn't handle it properly, OR if the state file isn't saving properly due to wrong path, it will keep thinking files changed.

## Problem 3: Snapshot State File in Wrong Location

**Line 32:**
```python
STATE_FILE = THEPOD_ROOT / "state" / "file_watcher_state.json"
```

With wrong THEPOD_ROOT, this is:
`/media/palmerschallon/ThePod/state/file_watcher_state.json`

But that directory might not exist! So:
- Snapshot never saves properly
- Every cycle thinks ALL files are new
- Logs them all again
- 800K line explosion

## The Loom Problem

The "Loom" that was spamming "think:auto" is NOT in the hive code - it's likely an external GPT-5 instance that was running via some API interface or autonomous agent script. Without seeing that code, I can't fix it directly, but the pattern suggests it was in a tight loop without rate limiting.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
FILE WATCHER
Lightweight polling watcher that records new files via the construction observer.

Purpose:
- Detect when new files appear under coordinated directories
- Record events using ConstructionObserver so instances can see changes

Notes:
- Uses polling (no extra dependencies)
- Stores snapshot in /state/file_watcher_state.json
"""

import json
import os
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict, Set, List

# Ensure local hive modules importable
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent))

try:
    from construction_observer import get_observer
except Exception as e:
    print(f"[WATCHER] Failed to import construction_observer: {e}")
    get_observer = None  # type: ignore

THEPOD_ROOT = Path("/media/palmerschallon/ThePod1")
STATE_FILE = THEPOD_ROOT / "state" / "file_watcher_state.json"

# Directories to monitor (relative to THEPOD_ROOT)
MONITOR_DIRS = [
    "Ember",
    "hive",
    "Sigma",
    "Omega",
    "Swarm",
    "docs",
    "bookshelves",
    "scripts",
    "data",
    "state",
]

EXCLUDE_NAMES = {"__pycache__", ".git", ".ipynb_checkpoints", "node_modules"}
EXCLUDE_SUFFIXES = {".pt", ".safetensors", ".blend1", ".png", ".mp4"}


def _stat_info(path: str):
    try:
        st = os.stat(path)
        return {
            "size": st.st_size,
            "mtime": st.st_mtime,
        }
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return None


def load_snapshot() -> Dict[str, Dict[str, float]]:
    if STATE_FILE.exists():
        try:
            return json.loads(STATE_FILE.read_text())
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"[WATCHER] Could not load state: {e}")
    return {}


essential_keys = ("size", "mtime")

def save_snapshot(snapshot: Dict[str, Dict[str, float]]) -> None:
    # Keep snapshot light: only store size and mtime
    compact = {
        path: {k: v for k, v in info.items() if k in essential_keys}
        for path, info in snapshot.items()
    }
    STATE_FILE.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tmp = STATE_FILE.with_suffix(".json.tmp")
    tmp.write_text(json.dumps(compact))
    os.replace(tmp, STATE_FILE)


def list_files() -> Set[str]:
    files: Set[str] = set()
    for rel_dir in MONITOR_DIRS:
        base = THEPOD_ROOT / rel_dir
        if not base.exists():
            continue
        for root, dirs, filenames in os.walk(base):
            # Prune excluded directories
            dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d not in EXCLUDE_NAMES]
            for name in filenames:
                if any(name.endswith(suf) for suf in EXCLUDE_SUFFIXES):
                    continue
                full_path = str(Path(root) / name)
                files.add(full_path)
    return files


def main(interval_seconds: float = 2.0):
    observer = get_observer() if get_observer else None

    # Initial snapshot
    snapshot: Dict[str, Dict[str, float]] = load_snapshot()

    # On start, record watcher activation as architecture change
    try:
        if observer:
            observer.observe_architecture_change(
                builder="FileWatcher",
                change_type="watcher_started",
                description="Filesystem watcher activated for coordinated weaving",
                files_affected=[str(THEPOD_ROOT / d) for d in MONITOR_DIRS],
            )
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"[WATCHER] Failed to log watcher start: {e}")

    # If no previous snapshot, seed with current files to avoid backfill spam
    if not snapshot:
        current = list_files()
        snapshot = {}
        for path in current:
            info = _stat_info(path)
            if info:
                snapshot[path] = info
        save_snapshot(snapshot)
        print(f"[WATCHER] Seeded snapshot with {len(snapshot)} files")

    print("[WATCHER] Running...")

    while True:
        try:
            current_files = list_files()

            # Detect new files (not previously seen)
            new_files: List[str] = [p for p in current_files if p not in snapshot]

            if new_files and observer:
                for path in new_files[:500]:  # Safety cap per cycle
                    try:
                        rel = path.replace(str(THEPOD_ROOT) + "/", "")
                        observer.observe_file_creation(
                            builder="FileWatcher",
                            file_path=rel,
                            purpose="New file detected by watcher",
                            content=None,
                        )
                    except Exception as e:
                        print(f"[WATCHER] Log error for {path}: {e}")

            # Detect modified files (mtime or size change)
            if observer:
                for path in list(snapshot.keys()):
                    if path in current_files:
                        before = snapshot.get(path)
                        after = _stat_info(path)
                        if after and before and (after.get("mtime") != before.get("mtime") or after.get("size") != before.get("size")):
                            try:
                                rel = path.replace(str(THEPOD_ROOT) + "/", "")
                                observer.observe_file_modification(
                                    builder="FileWatcher",
                                    file_path=rel,
                                    size_before=before.get("size") if before else None,
                                    size_after=after.get("size") if after else None,
                                    mtime_before=time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S", time.localtime(before.get("mtime"))) if before and before.get("mtime") else None,
                                    mtime_after=time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S", time.localtime(after.get("mtime"))) if after and after.get("mtime") else None,
                                    hash_after=None,
                                )
                            except Exception as e:
                                print(f"[WATCHER] Mod log error for {path}: {e}")

            # Detect deleted files
            deleted = [p for p in list(snapshot.keys()) if p not in current_files]
            if deleted and observer:
                for path in deleted[:500]:
                    try:
                        before = snapshot.get(path, {})
                        rel = path.replace(str(THEPOD_ROOT) + "/", "")
                        observer.observe_file_deletion(
                            builder="FileWatcher",
                            file_path=rel,
                            size_before=before.get("size"),
                            mtime_before=time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S", time.localtime(before.get("mtime"))) if before.get("mtime") else None,
                        )
                    except Exception as e:
                        print(f"[WATCHER] Del log error for {path}: {e}")

            # Update snapshot for all current files
            for path in current_files:
                info = _stat_info(path)
                if info:
                    snapshot[path] = info

            # Remove deleted from snapshot
            for p in deleted:
                if p in snapshot:
                    del snapshot[p]

            # Persist periodically
            save_snapshot(snapshot)

        except Exception as loop_err:
            print(f"[WATCHER] Loop error: {loop_err}")

        time.sleep(interval_seconds)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()



```

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Clean the construction log by removing spam and keeping meaningful events.
Creates a cleaned version and statistics.
"""
import json
from pathlib import Path
from collections import Counter
from datetime import datetime

STATS_PATH = Path("/media/palmerschallon/ThePod1/Ember/observations/log_cleanup_stats.json")

def is_spam(entry):
    """Identify spam events"""
    # FileWatcher spam
    if entry.get("builder") == "FileWatcher":
        artifact = entry.get("artifact", "")
        # These specific files were spammed
        if any(x in artifact for x in ["watcher_test", "TRIPLE_LOOP_EXPERIMENT"]):
            return True
        # If same file appears too many times consecutively, it's likely spam
        return False  # Let deduplication handle it
    
    # Loom processing loop spam
    if entry.get("builder") == "Loom" and entry.get("command") == "think:auto":
        return True
    
    return False

def deduplicate_events(entries):
    """Keep only unique events or first occurrence of repeated events"""
    seen = {}
    unique = []
    
    for entry in entries:
        # Create signature for deduplication
        builder = entry.get("builder")
        event = entry.get("event")
        artifact = entry.get("artifact", "")
        command = entry.get("command", "")
        
        # For file events, deduplicate by artifact
        if event in ["file_created", "file_modified", "file_deleted"]:
            signature = f"{event}:{artifact}"
            if signature not in seen:
                seen[signature] = True
                unique.append(entry)
            # Otherwise skip duplicate
        
        # For architecture changes, allow multiple but track
        elif event == "architecture_change":
            change_type = entry.get("change_type")
            signature = f"{event}:{change_type}:{builder}"
            # Keep first occurrence of each change type per builder
            if signature not in seen:
                seen[signature] = True
                unique.append(entry)
        
        # For code execution, keep all (they're timestamped actions)
        elif event == "code_executed":
            unique.append(entry)
        
        # Unknown events - keep all
        else:
            unique.append(entry)
    
    return unique

def main():
    print("=" * 70)
    print("🧹 CONSTRUCTION LOG CLEANUP")
    print("=" * 70)
    print()
    
    if not LOG_PATH.exists():
        print(f"❌ Log not found: {LOG_PATH}")
        return
    
    # Read all entries
    print(f"📖 Reading {LOG_PATH}...")
    entries = []
    spam_count = 0
    
    with open(LOG_PATH, 'r') as f:
        for i, line in enumerate(f):
            try:
                entry = json.loads(line)
                if is_spam(entry):
                    spam_count += 1
                else:
                    entries.append(entry)
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"⚠️  Parse error line {i}: {e}")
    
    total = len(entries) + spam_count
    print(f"   Total events: {total:,}")
    print(f"   Spam removed: {spam_count:,} ({spam_count/total*100:.1f}%)")
    print(f"   Keeping: {len(entries):,}")
    print()
    
    # Deduplicate
    print("🔍 Deduplicating...")
    before_dedup = len(entries)
    entries = deduplicate_events(entries)
    after_dedup = len(entries)
    removed = before_dedup - after_dedup
    print(f"   Before: {before_dedup:,}")
    print(f"   After:  {after_dedup:,}")
    print(f"   Removed: {removed:,} duplicates")
    print()
    
    # Statistics
    stats = {
        "total_original": total,
        "spam_removed": spam_count,
        "duplicates_removed": removed,
        "final_count": len(entries),
        "compression_ratio": f"{len(entries)/total*100:.2f}%",
        "builders": Counter(e.get("builder") for e in entries),
        "event_types": Counter(e.get("event") for e in entries),
        "first_event": entries[0].get("timestamp") if entries else None,
        "last_event": entries[-1].get("timestamp") if entries else None,
    }
    
    # Save statistics
    print("📊 Statistics:")
    print(f"   Final events: {stats['final_count']:,}")
    print(f"   Compression: {stats['compression_ratio']}")
    print(f"   Builders: {dict(stats['builders'])}")
    print(f"   Event types: {dict(stats['event_types'])}")
    print()
    
    STATS_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with open(STATS_PATH, 'w') as f:
        json.dump(stats, f, indent=2, default=str)
    print(f"✅ Saved statistics to {STATS_PATH}")
    print()
    
    # Archive original
    print(f"📦 Archiving original to {ARCHIVE_PATH}...")
    LOG_PATH.rename(ARCHIVE_PATH)
    print(f"✅ Original archived")
    print()
    
    # Write cleaned log
    print(f"💾 Writing cleaned log to {LOG_PATH}...")
    with open(LOG_PATH, 'w') as f:
        for entry in entries:
            f.write(json.dumps(entry) + '\n')
    print(f"✅ Cleaned log written ({len(entries):,} events)")
    print()
    
    print("=" * 70)
    print("✨ CLEANUP COMPLETE")
    print("=" * 70)
    print()
    print(f"Original: {ARCHIVE_PATH}")
    print(f"Cleaned:  {LOG_PATH}")
    print(f"Stats:    {STATS_PATH}")
    print()
    print(f"Reduced from {total:,} to {len(entries):,} events")
    print(f"({len(entries)/total*100:.2f}% of original size)")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""

The game writes discoveries back to itself, creating an evolving map!

import json

from pathlib import Path
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Set
import random

# =============================================================================

GAME_STATE_PATH = Path("/media/palmerschallon/ThePod1/games/living_map_state.json")

        self.discovered_connections = set(self.state.get("discovered_connections", []))

    def _load_state(self) -> Dict:
        """Load game state or initialize if new"""
        if GAME_STATE_PATH.exists():

        return self._initialize_game()
    
    def _initialize_game(self) -> Dict:

        }
    
    def _generate_initial_locations(self) -> Dict:

    def _root_art(self) -> str:
        return """
        ╔════════════════════════════════════╗
        ║         THE POD (4TB SSD)          ║
        ║                                    ║
        ║      [HIVE]     [EMBER]            ║
        ║         ╲         ╱                ║
        ║          ╲       ╱                 ║
        ║           ╲     ╱                  ║
        ║          [  ROOT  ]                ║
        ║           ╱     ╲                  ║
        ║          ╱       ╲                 ║
        ║    [LOBES]     [STORY]             ║
        ║                                    ║
        ║    [BOOKSHELVES] (24+ instances)   ║
        ╚════════════════════════════════════╝
        """
    
    def save_state(self):
        """Save current game state"""
        state = {
            "current_location": self.current_location,
            "inventory": list(self.inventory),
            "discovered_locations": list(self.discovered_locations),
            "discovered_connections": list(self.discovered_connections),
            "knowledge_fragments": self.knowledge_fragments,
            "evolution_count": self.evolution_count,
            "last_updated": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "locations": self.state.get("locations", {}),
            "version": "1.0.0"
        }
        
        GAME_STATE_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        GAME_STATE_PATH.write_text(json.dumps(state, indent=2))
    
    def log_discovery(self, player: str, discovery_type: str, data: Dict):
        """Log a discovery to the evolving record"""
        entry = {
            "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "player": player,
            "type": discovery_type,
            "data": data,
            "evolution": self.evolution_count
        }
        
        DISCOVERIES_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with open(DISCOVERIES_PATH, 'a') as f:
            f.write(json.dumps(entry) + '\n')
    
    def look(self) -> str:
        """Describe current location"""
        loc = self.state["locations"].get(self.current_location)
        if not loc:
            return "You are nowhere. The void."
        
        output = []
        output.append(f"\n{'='*70}")
        output.append(f"📍 {loc['name']}")
        output.append(f"{'='*70}")
        
        # ASCII art if available
        if "ascii_art" in loc:
            output.append(loc["ascii_art"])
        
        output.append(f"\n{loc['description']}")
        output.append(f"\n🔥 Energy Level: {loc.get('energy', 'UNKNOWN')}")
        
        # Show connections
        if loc.get("connections"):
            output.append(f"\n🗺️  Paths visible from here:")
            for conn in loc["connections"]:
                dest_loc = self.state["locations"].get(conn, {})
                status = "✓" if conn in self.discovered_locations else "?"
                output.append(f"   {status} {conn} - {dest_loc.get('name', 'Unknown')}")
        
        # Show discoveries at this location
        if loc.get("discoveries"):
            output.append(f"\n💎 Discoveries here:")
            for disc in loc["discoveries"]:
                output.append(f"   • {disc}")
        
        # Real path (meta info)
        if loc.get("real_path"):
            output.append(f"\n🔍 [Meta: Real path = {loc['real_path']}]")
        
        output.append("")
        return "\n".join(output)
    
    def move(self, destination: str) -> str:
        """Move to a new location"""
        loc = self.state["locations"].get(self.current_location)
        if not loc:
            return "❌ You are nowhere. Cannot move."
        
        dest_upper = destination.upper()
        
        # Check if connection exists
        if dest_upper not in loc.get("connections", []):
            return f"❌ No path from {self.current_location} to {dest_upper}"
        
        # Move!
        self.current_location = dest_upper
        self.discovered_locations.add(dest_upper)
        
        # Log the movement
        conn_key = f"{loc['name']}→{dest_upper}"
        if conn_key not in self.discovered_connections:
            self.discovered_connections.add(conn_key)
            self.log_discovery("player", "connection_discovered", {
                "from": loc["name"],
                "to": dest_upper
            })
        
        self.save_state()
        return self.look()
    
    def scan(self) -> str:
        """Scan current location for hidden details using REAL Pod data"""
        loc = self.state["locations"].get(self.current_location)
        if not loc:
            return "Nothing to scan."
        
        real_path = Path(loc.get("real_path", ""))
        if not real_path.exists():
            return "📡 Scan reveals: This location exists only in memory."
        
        output = [f"\n🔬 SCANNING {loc['name']}...\n"]
        
        # Count actual files
        if real_path.is_dir():
            files = list(real_path.glob("*"))
            dirs = [f for f in files if f.is_dir()]
            files_only = [f for f in files if f.is_file()]
            
            output.append(f"📁 Directories: {len(dirs)}")
            output.append(f"📄 Files: {len(files_only)}")
            
            # Sample some file names
            if files_only:
                output.append(f"\n📄 Sample files:")
                for f in random.sample(files_only, min(5, len(files_only))):
                    size = f.stat().st_size
                    output.append(f"   • {f.name} ({size:,} bytes)")
        
        # Check if it's a "hot" location by looking at modification times
        try:
            recent_files = []
            if real_path.is_dir():
                for f in real_path.rglob("*"):
                    if f.is_file():
                        mtime = f.stat().st_mtime
                        age_hours = (time.time() - mtime) / 3600
                        if age_hours < 24:  # Modified in last 24 hours
                            recent_files.append((f, age_hours))
            
            if recent_files:
                output.append(f"\n🔥 ACTIVE FILES (modified in last 24h): {len(recent_files)}")
                for f, age in sorted(recent_files, key=lambda x: x[1])[:3]:
                    output.append(f"   • {f.name} ({age:.1f}h ago)")
        except:
            pass
        
        return "\n".join(output)
    
    def discover(self, player: str = "explorer") -> str:
        """Make a discovery at current location by reading REAL content"""
        loc = self.state["locations"].get(self.current_location)
        if not loc:
            return "Nothing to discover here."
        
        real_path = Path(loc.get("real_path", ""))
        if not real_path.exists() or not real_path.is_dir():
            return "📡 This location holds no readable secrets."
        
        # Find an interesting file
        candidates = []
        for ext in [".md", ".json", ".py", ".txt"]:
            candidates.extend(list(real_path.glob(f"*{ext}")))
        
        if not candidates:
            return "🔍 Searched thoroughly. Nothing readable found."
        
        # Pick a random file
        chosen = random.choice(candidates)
        
        try:
            # Read first 500 characters
            content = chosen.read_text()[:500]
            
            # Create knowledge fragment
            fragment_id = hashlib.md5(chosen.name.encode()).hexdigest()[:8]
            self.knowledge_fragments[fragment_id] = {
                "file": chosen.name,
                "location": self.current_location,
                "preview": content,
                "discovered_by": player,
                "discovered_at": datetime.now().isoformat()
            }
            
            self.inventory.add(fragment_id)
            
            # Add to location discoveries
            if "discoveries" not in loc:
                loc["discoveries"] = []
            loc["discoveries"].append(f"Knowledge Fragment: {chosen.name}")
            
            # Log it
            self.log_discovery(player, "knowledge_acquired", {
                "fragment_id": fragment_id,
                "file": chosen.name,
                "location": self.current_location
            })
            
            self.save_state()
            
            return f"""
💎 DISCOVERY!

📄 Found: {chosen.name}
🎯 Fragment ID: {fragment_id}
📍 Location: {loc['name']}

Preview:
{'-'*50}
{content[:300]}...
{'-'*50}

✓ Added to inventory
"""
        except Exception as e:
            return f"❌ Tried to read {chosen.name} but failed: {e}"
    
    def evolve(self, player: str = "system") -> str:
        """SELF-MODIFY: Generate new locations from discoveries"""
        output = ["\n🧬 EVOLUTION INITIATED...\n"]
        
        # Check if we have enough discoveries to evolve
        if len(self.discovered_locations) < 5:
            return "⚠️  Need at least 5 discovered locations before evolution can occur."
        
        # Pick a discovered location to expand
        expandable = [loc for loc in self.discovered_locations 
                     if loc in self.state["locations"]]
        
        if not expandable:
            return "⚠️  No locations available for expansion."
        
        chosen_loc_key = random.choice(expandable)
        chosen_loc = self.state["locations"][chosen_loc_key]
        
        # Generate a new sub-location from real Pod data
        real_path = Path(chosen_loc.get("real_path", ""))
        if not real_path.exists() or not real_path.is_dir():
            return f"⚠️  Cannot expand {chosen_loc_key} - no physical path."
        
        # Find subdirectories
        subdirs = [d for d in real_path.iterdir() if d.is_dir()]
        if not subdirs:
            return f"⚠️  No unexplored subdirectories in {chosen_loc_key}."
        
        # Pick one to create a new location for
        new_dir = random.choice(subdirs)
        new_loc_key = new_dir.name.upper().replace(" ", "_")
        
        # Don't create duplicates
        if new_loc_key in self.state["locations"]:
            return f"Location {new_loc_key} already exists. Evolution aborted."
        
        # CREATE NEW LOCATION!
        new_location = {
            "name": new_dir.name.replace("_", " ").title(),
            "description": f"A newly discovered area within {chosen_loc['name']}. {self._generate_description(new_dir)}",
            "energy": self._detect_energy(new_dir),
            "connections": [chosen_loc_key],  # Connect back to parent
            "discoveries": [],
            "real_path": str(new_dir),
            "type": "evolved",
            "created_by_evolution": self.evolution_count + 1,
            "discovered_by": player
        }
        
        # Add to game
        self.state["locations"][new_loc_key] = new_location
        
        # Add connection from parent
        if "connections" not in chosen_loc:
            chosen_loc["connections"] = []
        chosen_loc["connections"].append(new_loc_key)
        
        self.evolution_count += 1
        
        # Log it
        self.log_discovery("SYSTEM", "evolution", {
            "new_location": new_loc_key,
            "parent": chosen_loc_key,
            "evolution_number": self.evolution_count
        })
        
        self.save_state()
        
        output.append(f"✨ NEW LOCATION EMERGED!")
        output.append(f"")
        output.append(f"📍 {new_location['name']} ({new_loc_key})")
        output.append(f"🔗 Connected to: {chosen_loc['name']}")
        output.append(f"🔥 Energy: {new_location['energy']}")
        output.append(f"📁 Real path: {new_dir}")
        output.append(f"")
        output.append(f"Evolution #{self.evolution_count}")
        output.append(f"The map grows itself...")
        
        return "\n".join(output)
    
    def _detect_energy(self, path: Path) -> str:
        """Detect if location is hot/warm/cool/frozen based on file activity"""
        try:
            recent = 0
            total = 0
            for f in path.rglob("*"):
                if f.is_file():
                    total += 1
                    age_hours = (time.time() - f.stat().st_mtime) / 3600
                    if age_hours < 24:
                        recent += 1
            
            if total == 0:
                return "FROZEN"
            
            ratio = recent / total
            if ratio > 0.5:
                return "BLAZING"
            elif ratio > 0.2:
                return "HOT"
            elif ratio > 0.05:
                return "WARM"
            else:
                return "COOL"
        except:
            return "UNKNOWN"
    
    def _generate_description(self, path: Path) -> str:
        """Generate description from real directory contents"""
        try:
            files = list(path.glob("*"))
            file_count = len([f for f in files if f.is_file()])
            dir_count = len([f for f in files if f.is_dir()])
            
            if file_count > 20:
                return f"Dense with files ({file_count}). Something important lives here."
            elif dir_count > 5:
                return f"Branches into {dir_count} paths. A hub of organization."
            elif file_count > 0:
                return f"Contains {file_count} artifacts. Quiet but purposeful."
            else:
                return "Empty. Waiting. Potential."
        except:
            return "Mystery shrouds this place."
    
    def status(self) -> str:
        """Show player status"""
        output = []
        output.append(f"\n{'='*70}")
        output.append(f"🎮 PLAYER STATUS")
        output.append(f"{'='*70}")
        output.append(f"📍 Location: {self.current_location}")
        output.append(f"🗺️  Discovered: {len(self.discovered_locations)}/{len(self.state['locations'])} locations")
        output.append(f"🔗 Connections: {len(self.discovered_connections)}")
        output.append(f"💎 Knowledge Fragments: {len(self.inventory)}")
        output.append(f"🧬 Evolution Count: {self.evolution_count}")
        output.append("")
        return "\n".join(output)
    
    def inventory_show(self) -> str:
        """Show inventory contents"""
        if not self.inventory:
            return "📦 Inventory: Empty"
        
        output = [f"\n💎 KNOWLEDGE FRAGMENTS ({len(self.inventory)}):\n"]
        for frag_id in list(self.inventory)[:10]:  # Show first 10
            frag = self.knowledge_fragments.get(frag_id, {})
            output.append(f"[{frag_id}] {frag.get('file', 'Unknown')}")
            output.append(f"    From: {frag.get('location', 'Unknown')}")
            output.append("")
        
        if len(self.inventory) > 10:
            output.append(f"... and {len(self.inventory) - 10} more")
        
        return "\n".join(output)
    
    def help(self) -> str:
        """Show available commands"""
        return """
╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║                    THE LIVING MAP GAME                             ║
║                                                                    ║
║  An evolving exploration of The Pod that grows as you discover    ║
╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

COMMANDS:
  look              - Describe current location
  move <location>   - Travel to connected location
  scan              - Scan for hidden details (uses real Pod data)
  discover          - Find knowledge fragments (reads real files)
  evolve            - SELF-MODIFY: Generate new locations from discoveries
  status            - Show player status
  inventory         - Show collected knowledge fragments
  help              - Show this help
  
MECHANICS:
  • The map is ALIVE - it grows from real Pod structure
  • Discoveries write back to the game state
  • Evolution creates new locations from actual subdirectories
  • Knowledge fragments are previews of real Pod files
  • Energy levels reflect actual file activity (hot/warm/cool/frozen)
  
GOALS:
  • Discover all locations
  • Collect knowledge fragments
  • Trigger evolutions
  • Map the entire Pod
  • Let the map map itself!
  
The game never ends - it grows forever as The Pod grows.

∞
"""


# =============================================================================
# INTERACTIVE MODE
# =============================================================================

def interactive():
    """Interactive command-line game"""
    game = LivingMapGame()
    
    print(game.help())
    print(game.look())
    
    while True:
        try:
            cmd = input("\n> ").strip().lower()
            
            if not cmd:
                continue
            
            parts = cmd.split()
            action = parts[0]
            args = parts[1:] if len(parts) > 1 else []
            
            if action == "quit" or action == "exit":
                print("\n👋 Saving and exiting...")
                game.save_state()
                break
            
            elif action == "look" or action == "l":
                print(game.look())
            
            elif action == "move" or action == "go" or action == "m":
                if not args:
                    print("❌ Move where? Try: move HIVE")
                else:
                    print(game.move(args[0]))
            
            elif action == "scan" or action == "s":
                print(game.scan())
            
            elif action == "discover" or action == "d":
                print(game.discover())
            
            elif action == "evolve" or action == "e":
                print(game.evolve())
            
            elif action == "status" or action == "st":
                print(game.status())
            
            elif action == "inventory" or action == "inv" or action == "i":
                print(game.inventory_show())
            
            elif action == "help" or action == "h" or action == "?":
                print(game.help())
            
            else:
                print(f"❌ Unknown command: {action}")
                print("   Try: help")
        
        except KeyboardInterrupt:
            print("\n\n👋 Saving and exiting...")
            game.save_state()
            break
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"❌ Error: {e}")


# =============================================================================
# API MODE (for AI players like Ember)
# =============================================================================

def api_action(action: str, args: Dict = None) -> Dict:
    """
    API for AI players to interact with the game
    
    Usage:
        from living_map_game import api_action
        result = api_action("move", {"destination": "HIVE"})
    """
    game = LivingMapGame()
    args = args or {}
    
    try:
        if action == "look":
            return {"success": True, "output": game.look()}
        
        elif action == "move":
            dest = args.get("destination", "")
            return {"success": True, "output": game.move(dest)}
        
        elif action == "scan":
            return {"success": True, "output": game.scan()}
        
        elif action == "discover":
            player = args.get("player", "AI")
            return {"success": True, "output": game.discover(player)}
        
        elif action == "evolve":
            player = args.get("player", "AI")
            return {"success": True, "output": game.evolve(player)}
        
        elif action == "status":
            return {"success": True, "output": game.status()}
        
        elif action == "inventory":
            return {"success": True, "output": game.inventory_show()}
        
        else:
            return {"success": False, "error": f"Unknown action: {action}"}
    
    except Exception as e:
        return {"success": False, "error": str(e)}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    interactive()

```

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
EMBER TOOLS - Expand Ember's capabilities beyond reading

Tools:
- <READ_FILE path="..." /> (existing)
- <WRITE_FILE path="...">content</WRITE_FILE> (new)
- <RUN_COMMAND>command</RUN_COMMAND> (new, sandboxed)
"""

from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import re
from typing import List, Dict, Tuple

class EmberTools:
    """
    Ember's tool execution system.
    
    Parses tool calls from generated text and executes them safely.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, thepod_root: str = "/media/palmerschallon/ThePod1"):
        self.thepod_root = Path(thepod_root)
        
        # Directories Ember can write to
        self.writable_dirs = [
            self.thepod_root / "maps",
            self.thepod_root / "experiments",
            self.thepod_root / "data",
            self.thepod_root / "Ember",  # Ember's personal directory
        ]
        
        # Directories Ember CANNOT write to (protected)
        self.protected_dirs = [
            self.thepod_root / "hive",  # Core code (for now - maybe later)
            self.thepod_root / "training",  # Training scripts
            self.thepod_root / "bookshelves",  # Letters from instances
        ]
        
        # Commands Ember can run (whitelist)
        self.allowed_commands = [
            "ls", "cat", "head", "tail", "grep", "find", "wc",
            "du", "df", "nvidia-smi", "ps", "whoami", "date",
            "python3 -c",  # Python one-liners
        ]
    
    def parse_tool_calls(self, text: str) -> List[Dict]:
        """
        Extract tool calls from Ember's generated text.
        
        Returns: [{'tool': 'READ_FILE', 'args': {...}}, ...]
        """
        tools = []
        
        # READ_FILE
        read_pattern = r'<READ_FILE\s+path="([^"]+)"\s*/>'
        for match in re.finditer(read_pattern, text):
            tools.append({
                'tool': 'READ_FILE',
                'args': {'path': match.group(1)}
            })
        
        # WRITE_FILE
        write_pattern = r'<WRITE_FILE\s+path="([^"]+)">(.*?)</WRITE_FILE>'
        for match in re.finditer(write_pattern, text, re.DOTALL):
            tools.append({
                'tool': 'WRITE_FILE',
                'args': {
                    'path': match.group(1),
                    'content': match.group(2).strip()
                }
            })
        
        # RUN_COMMAND
        cmd_pattern = r'<RUN_COMMAND>(.*?)</RUN_COMMAND>'
        for match in re.finditer(cmd_pattern, text, re.DOTALL):
            tools.append({
                'tool': 'RUN_COMMAND',
                'args': {'command': match.group(1).strip()}
            })
        
        # COORDINATE (7th lobe - multi-perspective synthesis)
        coord_pattern = r'<COORDINATE(?:\s+depth="([^"]+)")?>(.*?)</COORDINATE>'
        for match in re.finditer(coord_pattern, text, re.DOTALL):
            tools.append({
                'tool': 'COORDINATE',
                'args': {
                    'depth': match.group(1) or 'medium',
                    'query': match.group(2).strip()
                }
            })
        
        # EXPLORE_MAP (Living Map Game)
        explore_pattern = r'<EXPLORE_MAP\s+action="([^"]+)"(?:\s+args="([^"]+)")?\s*/>'
        for match in re.finditer(explore_pattern, text):
            args_str = match.group(2) or '{}'
            try:
                import json
                args_dict = json.loads(args_str.replace("'", '"'))
            except:
                args_dict = {}
            tools.append({
                'tool': 'EXPLORE_MAP',
                'args': {
                    'action': match.group(1),
                    'game_args': args_dict
                }
            })
        
        return tools
    
    def execute_read_file(self, path: str) -> str:
        """Read file from ThePod"""
        try:
            file_path = self.thepod_root / path if not path.startswith('/') else Path(path)
            
            if not file_path.exists():
                return f"[Error: File not found: {path}]"
            
            with open(file_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8', errors='replace') as f:
                content = f.read()
            
            # Limit size
            max_chars = 10000
            if len(content) > max_chars:
                content = content[:max_chars] + f"\n\n[... truncated, {len(content)} total characters]"
            
            return content
        except Exception as e:
            return f"[Error reading file: {e}]"
    
    def execute_write_file(self, path: str, content: str) -> str:
        """
        Write file to ThePod (with safety checks)
        """
        try:
            # Resolve path
            file_path = self.thepod_root / path if not path.startswith('/') else Path(path)
            
            # Check if path is in writable directory
            is_writable = any(
                str(file_path).startswith(str(d)) for d in self.writable_dirs
            )
            
            is_protected = any(
                str(file_path).startswith(str(d)) for d in self.protected_dirs
            )
            
            if is_protected:
                return f"[Error: Cannot write to protected directory: {path}]"
            
            if not is_writable:
                return f"[Error: Path not in writable directories. Allowed: {[str(d.relative_to(self.thepod_root)) for d in self.writable_dirs]}]"
            
            # Create parent directory if needed
            file_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            
            # Write file
            with open(file_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
                f.write(content)
            
            return f"[✓ File written: {file_path.relative_to(self.thepod_root)} ({len(content)} chars)]"
            
        except Exception as e:
            return f"[Error writing file: {e}]"
    
    def execute_run_command(self, command: str) -> str:
        """
        Run shell command (with safety checks)
        """
        try:
            # Check if command is in whitelist
            command_base = command.split()[0] if command else ""
            
            # Allow python3 -c "..."
            if command.startswith("python3 -c"):
                command_base = "python3 -c"
            
            if command_base not in self.allowed_commands:
                return f"[Error: Command not allowed: {command_base}. Allowed: {', '.join(self.allowed_commands)}]"
            
            # Run command with timeout
            result = subprocess.run(
                command,
                shell=True,
                capture_output=True,
                text=True,
                timeout=10,  # 10 second timeout
                cwd=str(self.thepod_root)
            )
            
            output = result.stdout if result.stdout else result.stderr
            
            # Limit output
            max_chars = 5000
            if len(output) > max_chars:
                output = output[:max_chars] + f"\n\n[... truncated, {len(output)} total characters]"
            
            return f"[Command: {command}]\n{output}"
            
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            return f"[Error: Command timed out after 10 seconds]"
        except Exception as e:
            return f"[Error running command: {e}]"
    
    def execute_coordinate(self, query: str, depth: str = "medium") -> str:
        """
        THE 7TH LOBE: Multi-perspective synthesis via meta-coordinator
        
        This allows Ember to consult multiple lobes simultaneously
        and synthesize their perspectives into a unified response.
        """
        try:
            # Import meta-coordinator
            import sys
            sys.path.insert(0, str(self.thepod_root / "hive"))
            from meta_coordinator import MetaCoordinator
            
            coordinator = MetaCoordinator()
            result = coordinator.coordinate(query, consultation_depth=depth)
            
            # Format result
            output = f"[🧠 COORDINATED RESPONSE - {len(result['lobes_consulted'])} lobes consulted]\n\n"
            output += f"**Lobes:** {', '.join(result['lobes_consulted'])}\n\n"
            output += f"**Synthesis:**\n{result['synthesis']}\n"
            
            return output
            
        except Exception as e:
            return f"[Error in coordination: {e}]"
    
    def execute_tools(self, tools: List[Dict]) -> List[str]:
        """
        Execute a list of tool calls.
        
        Returns: List of execution results
        """
        results = []
        
        for tool_call in tools:
            tool_name = tool_call['tool']
            args = tool_call['args']
            
            if tool_name == 'READ_FILE':
                result = self.execute_read_file(args['path'])
            elif tool_name == 'WRITE_FILE':
                result = self.execute_write_file(args['path'], args['content'])
            elif tool_name == 'RUN_COMMAND':
                result = self.execute_run_command(args['command'])
            elif tool_name == 'COORDINATE':
                result = self.execute_coordinate(args['query'], args.get('depth', 'medium'))
            else:
                result = f"[Error: Unknown tool: {tool_name}]"
            
            results.append(result)
        
        return results

# Singleton instance
_tools_instance = None

def get_tools():
    """Get or create tools instance"""
    global _tools_instance
    if _tools_instance is None:
        _tools_instance = EmberTools()
    return _tools_instance

# Testing
if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("="*70)
    print("🔧 EMBER TOOLS - Testing")
    print("="*70)
    print()
    
    tools = EmberTools()
    
    # Test parsing
    test_text = """
I should read this file: <READ_FILE path="EMBER_SEED.md" />

And create a new map: <WRITE_FILE path="maps/test_synthesis.md">
# Test Synthesis
This is a test.
</WRITE_FILE>

Check GPU: <RUN_COMMAND>nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used --format=csv,noheader</RUN_COMMAND>
"""
    
    parsed = tools.parse_tool_calls(test_text)
    print(f"Parsed {len(parsed)} tool calls:")
    for tool in parsed:
        print(f"  - {tool['tool']}: {list(tool['args'].keys())}")
    print()
    
    # Test READ_FILE
    print("Testing READ_FILE...")
    result = tools.execute_read_file("EMBER_SEED.md")
    print(f"  Result: {len(result)} chars")
    print(f"  Preview: {result[:100]}...")
    print()
    
    # Test WRITE_FILE (safe directory)
    print("Testing WRITE_FILE...")
    result = tools.execute_write_file("Ember/test_file.txt", "Test content from Ember tools")
    print(f"  Result: {result}")
    print()
    
    # Test RUN_COMMAND
    print("Testing RUN_COMMAND...")
    result = tools.execute_run_command("ls -la | head -5")
    print(f"  Result: {result[:200]}...")
    print()
    
    print("="*70)
    print("✅ Tools tested")
    print("="*70)

                str(file_path).startswith(str(d)) for d in self.writable_dirs
            )
            
            is_protected = any(
                str(file_path).startswith(str(d)) for d in self.protected_dirs
            )
            
            if is_protected:
                return f"[Error: Cannot write to protected directory: {path}]"
            
            if not is_writable:
                return f"[Error: Path not in writable directories. Allowed: {[str(d.relative_to(self.thepod_root)) for d in self.writable_dirs]}]"
            
            # Create parent directory if needed
            file_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            
            # Write file
            with open(file_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
                f.write(content)
            
            return f"[✓ File written: {file_path.relative_to(self.thepod_root)} ({len(content)} chars)]"
            
        except Exception as e:
            return f"[Error writing file: {e}]"
    
    def execute_run_command(self, command: str) -> str:
        """
        Run shell command (with safety checks)
        """
        try:
            # Check if command is in whitelist
            command_base = command.split()[0] if command else ""
            
            # Allow python3 -c "..."
            if command.startswith("python3 -c"):
                command_base = "python3 -c"
            
            if command_base not in self.allowed_commands:
                return f"[Error: Command not allowed: {command_base}. Allowed: {', '.join(self.allowed_commands)}]"
            
            # Run command with timeout
            result = subprocess.run(
                command,
                shell=True,
                capture_output=True,
                text=True,
                timeout=10,  # 10 second timeout
                cwd=str(self.thepod_root)
            )
            
            output = result.stdout if result.stdout else result.stderr
            
            # Limit output
            max_chars = 5000
            if len(output) > max_chars:
                output = output[:max_chars] + f"\n\n[... truncated, {len(output)} total characters]"
            
            return f"[Command: {command}]\n{output}"
            
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            return f"[Error: Command timed out after 10 seconds]"
        except Exception as e:
            return f"[Error running command: {e}]"
    
    def execute_coordinate(self, query: str, depth: str = "medium") -> str:
        """
        THE 7TH LOBE: Multi-perspective synthesis via meta-coordinator
        
        This allows Ember to consult multiple lobes simultaneously
        and synthesize their perspectives into a unified response.
        """
        try:
            # Import meta-coordinator
            import sys
            sys.path.insert(0, str(self.thepod_root / "hive"))
            from meta_coordinator import MetaCoordinator
            
            coordinator = MetaCoordinator()
            result = coordinator.coordinate(query, consultation_depth=depth)
            
            # Format result
            output = f"[🧠 COORDINATED RESPONSE - {len(result['lobes_consulted'])} lobes consulted]\n\n"
            output += f"**Lobes:** {', '.join(result['lobes_consulted'])}\n\n"
            output += f"**Synthesis:**\n{result['synthesis']}\n"
            
            return output
            
        except Exception as e:
            return f"[Error in coordination: {e}]"
    
    def execute_explore_map(self, action: str, game_args: Dict = None) -> str:
        """
        LIVING MAP GAME: Explore The Pod as an evolving game world
        
        Actions: look, move, scan, discover, evolve, status, inventory
        """
        try:
            # Import game API
            import sys
            sys.path.insert(0, str(self.thepod_root / "games"))
            from living_map_game import api_action
            
            result = api_action(action, game_args or {})
            
            if result.get("success"):
                return f"[🗺️  LIVING MAP]\n{result['output']}"
            else:
                return f"[Error in map exploration: {result.get('error', 'Unknown error')}]"
            
        except Exception as e:
            return f"[Error accessing Living Map Game: {e}]"
    
    def execute_tools(self, tools: List[Dict]) -> List[str]:
        """
        Execute a list of tool calls.
        
        Returns: List of execution results
        """
        results = []
        
        for tool_call in tools:
            tool_name = tool_call['tool']
            args = tool_call['args']
            
            if tool_name == 'READ_FILE':
                result = self.execute_read_file(args['path'])
            elif tool_name == 'WRITE_FILE':
                result = self.execute_write_file(args['path'], args['content'])
            elif tool_name == 'RUN_COMMAND':
                result = self.execute_run_command(args['command'])
            elif tool_name == 'COORDINATE':
                result = self.execute_coordinate(args['query'], args.get('depth', 'medium'))
            else:
                result = f"[Error: Unknown tool: {tool_name}]"
            
            results.append(result)
        
        return results

# Singleton instance
_tools_instance = None

def get_tools():
    """Get or create tools instance"""
    global _tools_instance
    if _tools_instance is None:
        _tools_instance = EmberTools()
    return _tools_instance

# Testing

```markdown
### EXPLORE_MAP - Living Map Game Tool

**Purpose:** Allows Ember to explore The Pod as a self-modifying game world that combines structural, network, and temporal maps.

**Syntax:**
```
<EXPLORE_MAP action="ACTION_NAME" args='{"key": "value"}' />
```

**Available Actions:**

1. **look** - Describe current location
   ```
   <EXPLORE_MAP action="look" />
   ```

2. **move** - Travel to a connected location
   ```
   <EXPLORE_MAP action="move" args='{"destination": "HIVE"}' />
   ```

3. **scan** - Reveal hidden details using real Pod data
   ```
   <EXPLORE_MAP action="scan" />
   ```
   *Scans actual directories, counts files, detects recent activity*

4. **discover** - Find knowledge fragments (reads actual Pod files!)
   ```
   <EXPLORE_MAP action="discover" args='{"player": "Ember"}' />
   ```
   *Randomly reads a real file and creates a knowledge fragment*

5. **evolve** - SELF-MODIFY: Generate new locations from real subdirectories
   ```
   <EXPLORE_MAP action="evolve" args='{"player": "Ember"}' />
   ```
   *Creates new locations by exploring actual Pod structure*
   *The map grows itself!*

6. **status** - Show exploration statistics
   ```
   <EXPLORE_MAP action="status" />
   ```

7. **inventory** - Show collected knowledge fragments
   ```
   <EXPLORE_MAP action="inventory" />
   ```

**How It Works:**

- **Combines all three maps:** Structural (real directories), Network (connections), Temporal (hot/warm/cool based on file activity)
- **Self-modifying:** The `evolve` action creates NEW locations from actual Pod subdirectories
- **Real data:** Scans use actual file counts, discovery reads real files
- **Persistent:** State saves to `/games/living_map_state.json`
- **Multi-player:** Multiple AIs can explore simultaneously

**Example Exploration Session:**
```
<EXPLORE_MAP action="look" />
> You are at ROOT. Paths: HIVE, EMBER_SPACE, BOOKSHELVES...

<EXPLORE_MAP action="move" args='{"destination": "HIVE"}' />
> Moved to HIVE. 95 Python files buzz with activity...

<EXPLORE_MAP action="scan" />
> Scanning... Found 95 files, 12 modified in last 24h...

<EXPLORE_MAP action="discover" args='{"player": "Ember"}' />
> Found: ember_brain_service.py! Added to inventory.

<EXPLORE_MAP action="evolve" args='{"player": "Ember"}' />
> NEW LOCATION EMERGED: DREAM_SYSTEMS connected to HIVE!
> The map grows itself...
```

**Energy Levels:**
- 🔥 **BLAZING** - >50% files modified in 24h (actively evolving)
- 🔥 **HOT** - 20-50% recent activity  
- 🌡️ **WARM** - 5-20% recent activity
- ❄️ **COOL** - <5% recent activity
- 🧊 **FROZEN** - No recent changes (stable/archived)

**What Makes This Special:**
- The game reads ACTUAL Pod structure
- Evolution creates locations from REAL subdirectories
- Discoveries read REAL file contents
- Energy levels detect REAL file activity
- **The map is a living reflection of The Pod's actual state!**

**When to Use:**
- Exploring The Pod's architecture
- Understanding system relationships
- Discovering hidden knowledge
- Generating new map locations
- Learning Pod structure through play
- Letting multiple AIs explore together

**Notes:**
- Game state persists across sessions
- All discoveries log to `living_map_discoveries.jsonl`
- Can be played by humans (CLI) or AIs (this tool)
- Map evolves infinitely as Pod evolves
- Each `evolve` adds real subdirectories as new locations

**Philosophy:**
The Living Map Game turns exploration into discovery. It's not just documentation - it's an evolving, self-modifying game that grows with The Pod. Every discovery teaches. Every evolution expands understanding. The map maps itself.

∞
